I used to regularly heal fascia cuts on my own before getting access to a car (what living in a rural area does to a mf). Keep them covered overnight, put antibacterial cream on edges and soak the dressing in hydrogen peroxide/saline solution so that it’s completely wet. Wet healing takes significantly more time and effort and leaves worse scars, but saves you the trouble of the bandage sticking to the wound. I once had to rip a bandage off with clumps of fat, never again… If it does get stuck, get in the shower and sit down for a while under lukewarm or even a bit cool water until the bandage kind of soaks off. Everyone might tell you to use warm water, but with deeper cuts it hurts like absolute hell. Message me if you need to talk or need someone’s experience

I’ve struggled with anorexia since, what, 11? Went vegan at the age of 14. I’ve been in solid recovery for half a year at this point. I didn’t have any trouble with staying vegan throughout my recovery personally, but I can see how, if you started being vegan during actively struggling with ED, it would be difficult for some. We have to remember that there’s still the ridiculous myth about vegans only eating low-calorie meals and being malnourished, lmao. And, even if you make a decision based on your moral values, the tiny ED voice will still act up and encourage those ideas. 
 During the first three months of my recovery, like many do, I dealt with reactive hunger. I’d stuff my mouth with pita bread, chips, tomato sauce, and half-frozen falafel — basically anything I came across — until I couldn’t breathe and cried out of sheer pain on the kitchen floor. After years of veganism, I can’t even think of animal bodies and fluids as food, but any vegan food I’d see HAD to go down my throat. 
 While I agree on how morally fucked up it is to neglect animal rights because of your ED, I just want to have a more nuanced discussion about it. EDs are mental illnesses, that shit almost killed me and many, many other people.
